note: Wheat+rye combined (production/domestic_use, PM20 2024): 817,371t / 245,873t. Uses a yield-cancellation argument: if the same milling/baking yield applies uniformly to domestic and imported grain, it cancels out of the production/domestic-use ratio, so raw-grain self-sufficiency approximates bread self-sufficiency. High confidence in direction (comfortably self-sufficient); the exact magnitude is a proxy, not a measured bread-specific figure - no official comparator exists for this sub-item.

note: Phase 12 update: FAOSTAT 2022 filled the oats gap (238.1% self-sufficient, previously blank in the Phase 1 PM20 pull) and gave real human-food consumption weights (kg/capita/yr: rice 4.77, barley 7.78, oats 5.97) to split this category between rice (25.8% of the weighted total, 0% self-sufficient) and oats+barley porridge grains (74.2%, 210.4% self-sufficient combined). Weighted blend of those two parts alone: ~156.2%. Presented as an UPPER BOUND, not the resolved category figure, because pasta (durum wheat, ~0% self-sufficient like rice per PM20's 0% durum production) is still excluded -- FAOSTAT doesn't separate durum from bread wheat, so no consumption weight for pasta specifically was available. Since pasta's true self-sufficiency is very likely near 0%, folding it in could only pull the blended figure down, never up -- hence 'upper bound.' See PHASE12_NOTES.md and docs/methodology.md Section 8. Phase 13 verification: confirmed Estonia produces pasta domestically (Tartu Mill) using imported durum wheat -- Estonia grows abundant common/soft wheat but not durum, which per PIKK.ee needs a drier, more continental climate than Estonia has; ERR/Novaator (2024) confirms durum is only an experimental trial crop on one farm, not commercially tracked. Pasta manufacturing is domestic; the raw durum input is not. This confirms (rather than merely assumes) pasta's ~0% raw-material self-sufficiency. See PHASE13_NOTES.md.
PM20/PM31 2024: 74,668t / 117,283t = 63.7%. Official 5yr-avg: 70%. Close (single-year vs 5yr-avg effect, already flagged in PHASE1_NOTES.md); headline uses the midpoint.

note: Phase 8 (FAOSTAT 2022, Estonia) update: no Statistikaamet PM-series balance table exists for pulses/legumes, so this was carried as 'unknown - assumed low' through Phases 2-7. FAOSTAT's Pulses aggregate for 2022 shows Estonia is actually a LARGE NET EXPORTER: production 123kt vs. domestic supply 37kt = 332% self-sufficient in aggregate, driven almost entirely by field peas (95kt production, 558% self-sufficient) -- but field peas in Estonia are grown predominantly for animal feed and export, not as a fresh human-food pulse. FAOSTAT's own 'Beans' line (dry beans -- closer to what RTU011's 'legumes' survey category likely captures as a plate item) shows 0t domestic production, fully imported. So the honest updated picture is bimodal, not a single percentage: Estonia produces field peas in surplus (mostly not eaten domestically as a table legume), while human-food-relevant pulses (beans, lentils, chickpeas) appear to be ~0% domestically produced, closer to the original 'assumed low' guess for THAT specific slice. Presented as a range/qualitative finding rather than one number since RTU011's 'legumes' consumption category can't be matched to FAOSTAT's item-level split with confidence.
PM34 2024: exact match to the official figure. High confidence.

agri.ee 2026 fish consumption study: production+catch far exceeds domestic use, consistent with the official >200%/300% figure. Critical caveat carried from Phase 2: only ~15% of this resource stays in Estonia for human consumption - the rest is exported. A high self-sufficiency ratio here does not mean fish is actually eaten domestically at that rate.

Phase 1 flagged this exact assumption for a Phase 3 double-check against trade data that never happened until Phase 12. FAOSTAT 2022 (Estonia, 'Nuts and products'): 0 t production vs. ~32kt domestic supply = exactly 0%. No Statistikaamet table for culinary seeds or cocoa; PM37 covers oil-crop seeds (rapeseed/sunflower/soy), a different category (see food_group_crosswalk.csv). Assumed near-zero, unconfirmed.

PM37 2024: 96,075t / 138,562t. Rapeseed is Estonia's only real domestic oil crop. Yield-cancellation logic (same as bread, above): if oil-extraction yield is uniform across domestic and imported seed crushed in Estonia, it cancels from the ratio, so raw-seed self-sufficiency approximates refined-oil self-sufficiency. Breaks down if a meaningful share of Estonia's edible oil trade is in already-refined form rather than raw seed - PM37 can't distinguish this.

PM37 2024: 0t domestic production (106t raw bean imports only, per Phase 2's PM37 note); fully imported. Also does not capture the separate soybean-meal/protein-feed trade (Section 5.4's known thin spot).

Estonia has no domestic sugar beet/cane refining industry (last domestic sugar factory closed years ago; general knowledge, not independently re-verified this session). Web search in Phase 5 found no contradicting figure. High confidence for raw sugar specifically.

Chocolate/confectionery/snack-food manufacturing could have some Estonian value-add even using imported raw sugar/cocoa - 'self-sufficiency' isn't a coherent same-basis metric for a manufactured-goods category the way it is for raw agricultural output. Left unscored rather than forced into a percentage; treated as structurally import-dependent in the qualitative write-up regardless.

Statistikaamet publishes a full honey resource-and-use balance (PM29): production 1,313 t vs. human consumption 1,339 t (2024) = 98.1% self-sufficient. This table was pulled into data/raw/statistikaamet/PM29_honey_2024.csv back in Phase 1 but never wired into the model -- a plain oversight, not a data gap. Modeled as its own resolved subitem (independent-source basis, like Fish & seafood) rather than folded into the unresolved 'Sweets, snacks & discretionary (total)' pill. Phase 12 addition.
